title: Transpose a 3x4 matrix
starter:
%x  = buffer 12 dtype=f32 slot=0
%y  = buffer 12 dtype=f32 slot=1
# x is a 3x4 matrix, row-major. Store its 4x3 transpose, row-major.
%v  = load %x
%m  = reshape %v shape=[4 3]
%f  = reshape %m shape=[12]
%s  = store %y %f
%y1 = after %y %s
hints: Reshaping to `[4 3]` reads the same 12 numbers in the same order, just cut into rows of 3. A transpose moves numbers around.
Keep the 3x4 shape, then swap the two axes with `permute`.
`reshape [3 4]`, then `permute order=[1 0]` (shape 4x3), then `reshape [12]` and store. Element `[i][j]` of the result is `x[j][i]`.
explain: `reshape` never moves data: it reinterprets the same row-major sequence. `permute order=[1 0]` swaps the axes, so output `[i][j]` reads input `[j][i]`. The final `reshape [12]` lays the 4x3 result back out row-major for the flat buffer. The all-ones test is the one input where the starter's wrong answer happens to look right.
